He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns men's basketball|Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns]], winning the [[Lefty Driesell Award]] as the national college defensive player of the year in 2014. Payton was selected by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] with the 10th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] before being traded to the [[Orlando Magic]]. ==College career== Payton was an unheralded recruit from [[John Ehret High School]] in [[Jefferson Parish, Louisiana]]. He chose to attend [[Louisiana–Lafayette Ragin' Cajuns men's basketball|Louisiana–Lafayette]], and after a promising freshman season in [[2011–12 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2011–12]], Payton came into his own as a sophomore in 2012–13. He averaged 15.9 [[Points per game|points]], 5.6 [[Rebounds per game|rebounds]], 5.5 [[Assists per game|assists]] and 2.4 [[Steal (basketball)|steals]] per game and was named first team All-[[Sun Belt Conference]].{{cite web | title = Payton & Long Earn Sun Belt Basketball Honors | work = RaginCajuns.com | date = March 6, 2013| url = http://www.ragincajuns.com/news/2013/3/6/MBB_0306132026.aspx?path=mbball | access-date = May 6, 2014}} After his breakout sophomore season, Payton was a late addition to Team USA's U19 World Championships Trials Roster to compete in the [[2013 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]]. After making the team, Payton started in all nine games for Team USA, on a team loaded with talent including other players such as [[Marcus Smart]], [[Aaron Gordon]], [[Jahlil Okafor]] and [[Jarnell Stokes]]. The team ultimately defeated the Serbian team led by [[Vasilije Micić]] and won the gold medal, going 9–0 in the tournament. As a junior in [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14]], Payton emerged as one of the top defensive players in college basketball. He raised his averages to 19.2 points, 5.9 assists, 6.0 rebounds and 2.3 steals per game and led the Ragin' Cajuns to the [[2014 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2014 NCAA Tournament]]. He was again named first team All-Sun Belt and was the conference Defensive Player of the Year. At the end of the season, he was named the National Defensive Player of the Year by winning the Lefty Driesell Award.{{cite web | last = Iles | first = Trey | title = UL-Lafayette point guard Elfrid Payton wins Lefty Driesell Award | work = NOLA.com | date = April 21, 2014| url = http://www.nola.com/sports/index.ssf/2014/04/ul-lafayette_point_guard_elfri.html | access-date = May 5, 2014}} In April 2014, Payton declared for the NBA draft, forgoing his final year of college eligibility.{{cite web | title = UL-Lafayette's Elfrid Payton declares for the NBA draft Monday | work = NOLA.com | date = April 4, 2014| url = http://www.nola.com/sports/index.ssf/2014/04/ul-lafayettes_elfrid_payton_de.html | access-date = May 5, 2014}} ==Professional career== ===Orlando Magic (2014–2018)=== ====2014–15 season==== [[File:Elfrid Payton Layup.jpg|thumb|right|Payton in February 2015, attacking the basket against [[Pau Gasol]]]] On June 26, 2014, Payton was selected with the 10th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] on draft night for [[Dario Šarić]], a future first-round pick, and a future second-round pick.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2111319-dario-saric-reportedly-traded-from-magic-to-76ers-for-rights-to-elfrid-payton|title=Report: Magic Trade Saric to Sixers for Payton|first=Matt|last=Fitzgerald|website=[[Bleacher Report]] }} On July 2, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Magic.{{cite web |title=Magic Sign Gordon and Payton |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/magic-sign-gordon-and-payton |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 24, 2017 |date=July 2, 2017}} He made his NBA debut on October 29, 2014, in a loss to the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. On January 16, 2015, Payton had a season-best game with 22 points and 12 assists in a loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. He was subsequently named the Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for January and was named a Rising Stars Challenge participant.{{cite web |title=Payton Named January's Kia NBA Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/payton-named-januarys-kia-nba-eastern-conference-rookie-month |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 24, 2017 |date=February 4, 2015}}{{cite web|url=http://orlandomagicdaily.com/2015/01/28/victor-oladipo-elfrid-payton-headed-rising-stars-challenge/|title=Victor Oladipo, Elfrid Payton headed to Rising Stars Challenge|date=January 28, 2015|access-date=February 16, 2015|archive-date=February 16, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150216095601/http://orlandomagicdaily.com/2015/01/28/victor-oladipo-elfrid-payton-headed-rising-stars-challenge/|url-status=dead}} On March 18, he recorded his first career [[triple-double]] with 15 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds in a loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20150318/ORLDAL/gameinfo.html Nowitzki scores 25, Mavs hang on to beat lowly Magic 107–102] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151014065539/http://www.nba.com/games/20150318/ORLDAL/gameinfo.html |date=October 14, 2015 }}. Nba.com. Retrieved on July 24, 2017. With a second straight triple-double recorded by Payton on March 20, he became the first Magic player to post consecutive triple-doubles and the first NBA rookie to do it since [[Antoine Walker]], with the Boston Celtics in 1997. Payton's 22 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists helped the Magic claim a 111–104 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20150320/PORORL/gameinfo.html Trail Blazers at Magic – March 20, 2015 – Game Preview, Play by Play, Scores and Recap on]. Nba.com (March 20, 2015). Retrieved on July 24, 2017. ====2015–16 season==== On November 18, 2015, Payton scored a then career-high 24 points in a 104–101 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20151118/MINORL/gameinfo.html Minnesota Timberwolves vs Orlando Magic – November 18, 2015 – Game Preview, Play by Play, Scores and Recap on]. Nba.com (November 18, 2015). Retrieved on July 24, 2017. Payton appeared in 116 straight games to begin his career before a left ankle injury forced him to sit out four games in early January 2016. He returned to action on January 14 in London to face the [[Toronto Raptors]], coming off the bench for the first time in 2015–16 and recording four points and four rebounds in a 106–103 overtime loss.[http://www.nba.com/games/20160114/TORORL/gameinfo.html Toronto Raptors vs Orlando Magic – January 14, 2016 – Game Preview, Play by Play, Scores and Recap on]. Nba.com (January 14, 2016). Retrieved on July 24, 2017. On March 23, 2016, he recorded his third career triple-double with 20 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 118–102 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20160323/ORLDET/gameinfo.html Orlando Magic vs Detroit Pistons – March 23, 2016 – Game Preview, Play by Play, Scores and Recap on]. Nba.com (March 23, 2016). Retrieved on July 24, 2017. ====2016–17 season==== [[File:Elfrid Payton And Kyle Lowry (33001664566).jpg|thumb|right|Payton defending [[Kyle Lowry]] in February 2017]] On December 6, 2016, Payton scored 22 of his career-high 25 points in the first half of the Magic's 124–116 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899757|title=Magic overcome Wall's 52 points, beat Wizards 124–116|work=ESPN.com|date=December 6, 2016|access-date=December 6, 2016}} He bested that mark on December 13, 2016, recording career highs with 26 points and 14 assists in a 131–120 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899811|title=Payton has career highs in points and assists in Magic win|work=ESPN.com|date=December 13, 2016|access-date=December 13, 2016}} On January 14, 2017, he had a career-high 28 points and added nine rebounds and nine assists in a 114–107 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900025|title=Gordon Hayward helps Jazz beat Magic 114–107|work=ESPN.com|date=January 14, 2017|access-date=January 14, 2017}} On March 6, 2017, he had his first triple-double of the season with 16 points, 10 assists and 11 rebounds in a 113–105 loss to the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900330|title=Knicks rally in fourth quarter, beat Magic 113–105|work=ESPN.com|date=March 6, 2017|access-date=March 7, 2017}} Two days later, he had his second straight triple-double with 22 points, 14 rebounds and 14 assists in a 98–91 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900344|title=Payton's 2nd straight triple-double leads Magic over Bulls|work=ESPN.com|date=March 8, 2017|access-date=March 9, 2017}} On March 13, 2017, in a 120–115 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]], Payton had 13 points, 13 assists and 10 rebounds for his third triple-double of the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900392|title=Kings beat Magic 120–115 to snap eight-game losing streak|work=ESPN.com|date=March 13, 2017|access-date=March 14, 2017}} On March 24, he continued his impressive run with 14 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists in a 115–87 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]]. It was his fourth triple-double in 10 games and seventh of his career.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900469|title=Payton's triple-double helps Magic rout Pistons 115–87|work=ESPN.com|date=March 24, 2017|access-date=March 25, 2017}} Seven days later, he recorded a career-high 15 assists to go with 12 points and nine rebounds in a 117–116 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900524|title=Thomas, Celtics hold off Magic for 117–116 win|work=ESPN.com|date=March 31, 2017|access-date=April 1, 2017}} On April 1, he had 20 points, 11 assists and 11 rebounds for his fifth triple-double of the season in the Magic's 121–111 loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899396|title=Lopez leads Nets over Magic, 121–111|work=ESPN.com|date=April 1, 2017|access-date=April 2, 2017}} ====2017–18 season==== Payton missed eight games early on the season 2017–18 season because of a left hamstring injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974911|title=Magic end two-game losing streak with 112-99 win over Knicks|work=ESPN.com|date=November 8, 2017|access-date=November 8, 2017}} An important piece in the Magic's offense, he had 11 points and 11 assists in 29 minutes in his return on November 8, helping the team end a two-game losing streak with a 112–99 win over the [[New York Knicks]]. On November 22, he had a season-high 13 assists in a 124–118 loss to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975012|title=Butler ties season high with 26, Wolves beat Magic 124-118|work=ESPN.com|date=November 22, 2017|access-date=November 22, 2017}} On December 23, 2017, he scored a career-high 30 points in a 130–103 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975234|title=Scott scores 18 in Wizards' 130-103 win over Magic|work=ESPN.com|date=December 23, 2017|access-date=December 23, 2017}} ===Phoenix Suns (2018)=== On February 8, 2018, Payton was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for a 2018 second-round pick.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-aquire-elfrid-payton-orlando|title=Phoenix Suns Acquire Elfrid Payton from Orlando|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2018|access-date=February 8, 2018}} He made his debut for the Suns two days later, recording 19 points, nine assists and six rebounds in 35 minutes in a 123–113 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975578|title=Nuggets use big second-half run to beat Suns 123-113|work=ESPN.com|date=February 10, 2018|access-date=February 12, 2018}} In his second game for the Suns on February 12, Payton scored a game-high 29 points in a 129–83 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975592|title=Coach Kerr takes backseat in Warriors' 129-83 win over Suns|work=ESPN.com|date=February 12, 2018|access-date=February 12, 2018}} Two days later, he had a triple-double with 13 points, 11 rebounds and 12 assists in a 107–97 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975609|title=Jazz win 11th straight, beating Suns 107-97|work=ESPN.com|date=February 14, 2018|access-date=February 14, 2018}} On March 4, 2018, he had 11 points, 10 rebounds and a season-high 14 assists in a 113–112 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975689|title=Prince hits go-ahead 3 in closing seconds, Hawks beat Suns|work=ESPN.com|date=March 4, 2018|access-date=March 5, 2018}} It was his second triple-double in nine games with the Suns—his nine games needed with the team to record two triple-doubles are the fewest ever by a Suns player.{{cite web|author=Phoenix Suns Stats|url=https://twitter.com/SunsBballComm/status/970428997946322944|title=Elfrid Payton has his second triple-double...|work=Twitter|date=March 4, 2018|access-date=March 5, 2018}} ===New Orleans Pelicans (2018–2019)=== On July 9, 2018, Payton signed with his hometown team the [[New Orleans Pelicans]].{{cite web |title=Pelicans sign free agents Elfrid Payton and Julius Randle |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-free-agents-elfrid-payton-and-julius-randle |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 9, 2018 |date=July 9, 2018}} In his debut for the Pelicans in their season opener on October 17, 2018, Payton recorded 10 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 131–112 win over the [[Houston Rockets]]. Payton's minimalist triple-double made him the first player to record exactly 10 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a single game since March 2, 2013, when [[Kyle Lowry]] did it for Toronto. It was Payton's 11th career triple-double.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070215|title=Davis, Mirotic lead Pelicans past Rockets 131-112|work=ESPN.com|date=October 17, 2018|access-date=October 17, 2018}} On November 16, against the [[New York Knicks]], Payton returned to the lineup after missing nine games with a sprained right ankle, only to fracture a finger in his left hand after eight minutes on the court.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070903|title=Davis scores 43 points, Pelicans tally to beat Knicks|work=ESPN.com|date=November 16, 2018|access-date=November 17, 2018}} He was subsequently ruled out for approximately six weeks.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/elfrid-payton-injury-update-11-19-18|title=Elfrid Payton Injury Update|work=NBA.com|date=November 19, 2018|access-date=November 19, 2018}} He returned to action on December 31 against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] after a 22-game absence.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071222|title=Randle, Miller lead Pelicans past Wolves, 123-114|work=ESPN.com|date=December 31, 2018|access-date=January 1, 2019}} In his second game back on January 2, he scored 25 points in a 126–121 loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071233|title=Nets build big lead, hold off Davis, Pelicans 126-121|work=ESPN.com|date=January 2, 2019|access-date=January 3, 2019}} On March 10, he had 15 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 128–116 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071668|title=Kevin Huerter has 27 points as Hawks top Pelicans 128-116|work=ESPN.com|date=March 10, 2019|access-date=March 11, 2019}} On March 12, he
